data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Chemical agents, peels & baths_

**Class:** Aromatic alcohol — antiseptic, anaesthetic, keratocoagulant

## Mechanism of action
- Low concentration: antiseptic and topical anaesthetic (antipruritic in calamine with phenol)
- 88% phenol: keratocoagulation — denatures proteins instantly (paradoxically less penetration than 50%)
- Baker–Gordon formula (phenol + croton oil + septisol + water): deep peel

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chemical matricectomy for ingrown toenails (88% phenol, 3 × 30 s)
- Deep chemical peels for severe photoageing and wrinkles (Baker–Gordon — rarely now)
- Antipruritic in lotions (0.5–1%); cautery of small lesions

## Dose & formulations
- Matricectomy: tourniquet, apply 88% phenol to matrix with cotton tip for 3 × 30 s, then irrigate with alcohol

## Adverse effects
- Systemic absorption (deep peels): cardiac arrhythmias — ECG monitoring, IV hydration, treat in segments over 60–90 min; renal and hepatic toxicity
- Permanent hypopigmentation ('alabaster' skin) after deep peels, scarring, laryngeal oedema

## Contraindications
- Deep peels: cardiac, renal, hepatic disease; dark skin types

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Deep phenol peel → arrhythmia (ECG monitoring)
- 88% phenol for ingrown nail matricectomy

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Phenol — carbolic acid) and ch.31 (Phenol peels); Wolverton 4e ch.53. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
